method: KEYFRAME-FIRST: refs, then a free Nano Banana still per beat, then Frames to Video on Veo 3.1 Lite from each still. Motion + sound prompts only.
cast: two friends, a man and a woman, late 20s
setting_basis: A narrow old-city lane at night and a plain open-air dhaba bench with a copper pot of dal on a wood fire; the footage shows no real eatery, interior, name or signage, and makes no claim beyond what the script says.
look: Soft natural light, natural colour, anamorphic 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, soft film grain, photorealistic, cinematic. Faces are never in close-up and no one looks at the camera. A phone screen is only a soft glow, never legible. No other people. No music, no speech, no voiceover, no text, captions, logos or watermark.

en: One November evening we left the Golden Temple lanes starving, and twenty fronts promised the best dal.
Meera would take any free table, but I held out for a reason.
The reason was on NakshIQ: a family making the same dal since nineteen sixteen, in Amritsar since Partition.
In Chowk Passian their dal makhani simmers in a copper pot for eight to twelve hours.
The tip said cash only, no AC, and before one or after eight to dodge the queue.

We came just after eight with cash, and Meera stopped arguing after one spoonful.
Travel intelligence is one reason among twenty signs.
NakshIQ.
hi: नवंबर की एक शाम हम स्वर्ण मंदिर की गलियों से भूखे निकले, और बीस दुकानें सबसे अच्छी दाल का दावा कर रही थीं।
मीरा किसी भी खाली टेबल पर बैठ जाती, पर मैं एक वजह पर अड़ा रहा।
वजह NakshIQ पर मिली: एक परिवार जो उन्नीस सौ सोलह से वही दाल बना रहा है, बँटवारे के बाद से अमृतसर में।
चौक पसियां में उनकी दाल मखनी तांबे के बर्तन में आठ से बारह घंटे पकती है।
टिप में लिखा था सिर्फ़ कैश, AC नहीं, और लाइन से बचना है तो एक बजे से पहले या आठ के बाद आओ।

हम आठ के ठीक बाद कैश लेकर पहुँचे, और पहले चम्मच के बाद मीरा ने बहस बंद कर दी।
ट्रैवल इंटेलिजेंस है बीस बोर्डों के बीच एक सही वजह।
NakshIQ.

shot_notes: Evening in an old Amritsar lane near the Golden Temple: a man and a woman in their late 20s walk side by side, seen from behind, the lane otherwise empty.
The pair pause at a corner lit by warm shopfront bulbs, the woman gesturing ahead, faces turned away, no readable signage.
Close on a dark copper pot of dal simmering over a wood fire, steam rising.
The man's hand counts a few folded rupee notes beside a steel thali on a plain table.
Over-the-shoulder shot of the woman lifting a spoonful of dal makhani from a steel bowl, her face out of frame.
Wide shot of the two walking back down the quiet lane, small in the frame, warm evening light.
